title: Fake LastPass Authenticator Installer Abuses Microsoft-Signed Driver to Kill Antivirus and EDR
blurb: A trojanized installer drops a legitimately signed driver to disable AV/EDR at the kernel level (BYOVD), then deploys its payload unguarded.

title: Et Tu, MacBook? Unprivileged Keystroke Inference and Context Profiling via the Built-in IMU Side Channel
blurb: Researchers show a MacBook's built-in accelerometer/gyroscope, readable without special privileges, leaks enough vibration data to infer keystrokes and user context.

title: CISA alerts of active exploitation of three Linux kernel flaws
blurb: Three Linux kernel vulnerabilities are under active attack; CISA's KEV listing sets a federal patch deadline and signals real-world exploitation, not just theoretical risk.

title: Touch grass? Not when AMD has whittled down ray tracing memory usage by 98% for these hardware-sapping bushes and trees
blurb: AMD's new foliage BVH compression cuts ray-traced vegetation's VRAM footprint by 98%, tackling one of ray tracing's worst memory hogs.

title: Weeks before GTA 6, Rockstar Games imposes new guidelines that restrict mods for missions, maps, updated storylines, and third-party IP
blurb: Rockstar's new modding policy bans mission/map mods, map combinations, and unauthorized ports right before GTA 6's launch window, tightening control over its ecosystem.

title: How Virus-like 'Jumping Genes' Became Our Partners in Evolution
blurb:
Problem: Transposons ("jumping genes") make up nearly half the human genome, long dismissed as parasitic junk DNA.
Approach: Researchers traced transposon insertions across species, from McClintock's corn work to peppered-moth genomes, mapping when these elements reshaped genomes.
Result: One transposon in a peppered moth gene drove its 1819 shift to dark wings; transposons also built animal eyes, immune systems, and mammalian placentas, jumping between species nearly 1,000 times.
Why it matters: Transposons look less like invaders and more like coevolving partners hosts actively regulate, driving both rapid adaptation and genome regulation itself.
Glossary: Transposon - a DNA sequence that can move within a genome. Epigenetic control - regulating gene activity without changing DNA. Horizontal transfer - genes moving between species.

title: Circular mRNA helps cell factories make up to six times as much protein
blurb:
Problem: Bacterial mRNA lacks the caps and tails protecting it elsewhere, so it degrades in minutes, capping protein output.
Approach: Seoul National University built CRESEnT: self-splicing intron fragments arranged in reverse order so an mRNA's own ends join into a closed ring, no external enzymes needed.
Result: Circularized mRNA boosted protein output 5.95x and mRNA levels 3.95x versus linear controls, with 1.5-2.7x gains on compounds like lycopene, across three bacterial species.
Why it matters: Circular RNA resists degradation, having no open ends for RNases to grab — a drop-in yield boost for existing microbial drug and biofuel lines.
Glossary: mRNA - carries a gene's instructions to a cell's protein-making machinery. Self-splicing intron - an RNA segment that cuts and rejoins itself. RNase - an enzyme that degrades RNA.

title: The RP2350 Does 1080p
blurb: A build pushes RP2350 video output to a full 1080p signal, documenting the timing tricks needed to hit that resolution on a microcontroller.

title: DIY Router on x86 E-Waste: OpenWrt and OPNsense
blurb: A discarded x86 mini PC gets a second life as a router, with a documented comparison of OpenWrt and OPNsense on the same hardware.

title: Making a game for the GBA and PC from the same codebase
blurb: A developer documents the engine constraints needed to target the GBA's tiny hardware and a modern PC from one shared codebase.
